brief:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's attacks on Arab members of parliament risk rekindling the climate of incitement that preceded Yitzhak Rabin's 1995 assassination, Al Jazeera English reported. Critics warn that his rhetoric against Arab lawmakers echoes the inflammatory language that contributed to the former prime minister's killing at the hands of a right-wing extremist.

The comparison reflects growing concerns about political polarization and the dangers of dehumanizing language directed at elected officials. Rabin's death marked a watershed moment in Israeli politics, demonstrating how unchecked incitement can translate into deadly violence against high-ranking figures.
dek: His attacks on Arab lawmakers echo the incitement that preceded Rabin’s assassination and risk unleashing new violence.
title: Netanyahu's rhetoric toward Arab lawmakers mirrors Rabin assassination incitement
